subject: AWS Marketplace negative invoice & entity mapping clarification for NebulaOps
messages:
From: Priya Desai <accounts-payable@nebulaops.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Chen <sam.chen@amazon.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Negative invoice applied to our account - urgent hold request

Hi Marcus,

We've received an AWS Marketplace invoice (Invoice #031) that shows a negative charge of -$12,345 labeled "Marketplace Credit Adjustment". Attached: NebulaOps_AWS-Invoice-031-NEG.pdf.

Per our ledger this credit was expected to hit a different legal entity (NebulaOps-EU, tax id ending in 312). As a result, our finance team has put the corresponding payout on hold pending confirmation that the credit belongs to our billing entity for US transactions.

Can Redwood confirm the mapping between the Marketplace seller account and the legal entity that was credited? Specifically we need: 1) the original metering report or invoice JSON for the affected SKUs, 2) any internal entity mapping file, and 3) confirmation of whether the credit was issued by AWS or by Redwood as a pass-through.

We're trying to close our month-end and need a response by EOD PT Friday, 2025-07-25. If you need a call, Priya Desai (AP) is available this afternoon.

Thanks,
Priya Desai
Billing Manager, NebulaOps
attachments: NebulaOps_AWS-Invoice-031-NEG.pdf
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Priya Desai <accounts-payable@nebulaops.com>
Cc: Sam Chen <sam.chen@amazon.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 10:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Negative invoice applied to our account - urgent hold request

Hi Priya — thanks for flagging and sorry for the stress. Looping in our billing ops (Marissa), marketplace lead (Jonas), and tax/accounting (Naomi).

Quick summary of what we see on our side: the negative line appears to be an automated adjustment generated on July 20 tied to a duplicate SKU charge. It landed against the seller account id 9012345678. I'm asking AWS (cc Sam) to share the adjustment report and the original metering payload.

Internal next steps I propose (we'll confirm timelines once we have the AWS attachment):
- Marissa: prepare a provisional GL credit note tagged to NemulaOps_US (provisional until mapping is confirmed). Please include the invoice id and a reference to the marketplace case.
- Jonas: verify whether any downstream revenue recognition was impacted for Q2; if so we may need a small cut/promo reversal.
- Naomi: prep VAT/tax note if the credit should be reallocated to EU entity (we'll need tax id).

Priya — I'm attaching our internal entity mapping export (entity-mapping.csv) and will forward any AWS artifacts as soon as Sam sends them. For the hold, we recommend Redwood place a temporary payout freeze on the NebulaOps payout tranche until we confirm, then issue a corrected payout or a reallocation credit depending on the outcome.

Happy to hop on a quick 30m call with you, Sam and our ops team this afternoon.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Revenue Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
attachments: entity-mapping.csv
From: Sam Chen <sam.chen@amazon.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Priya Desai <accounts-payable@nebulaops.com>
Cc: aws-marketplace-support@amazon.com
Date: Wed, 23 Jul 2025 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Negative invoice applied to our account - urgent hold request

Hi all,

Thanks for the ping. Case AWS-3456 assigned. The negative line was an automated duplicate-detection credit issued by AWS Marketplace on 2025-07-20. Attached: aws-adjustment-report-3456.csv.

Details: the credit references seller account 9012345678 and original usage records for SKU: ml-infer-standard-16. It appears two distinct listings (owner-level and partner-managed) both reported metering for the same usage window; AWS applied a system adjustment to prevent double billing. 

Actionable items we can provide: 
- Full metering payload for the affected timestamps (JSON export)
- Confirmation the credit was generated by AWS (not by Redwood), and the case id for audit (AWS-3456).
- Guidance on reclaiming/reallocating the credit if both seller entities present conflicting legal entities.

I can share the JSON export to Marcus's S3 link or attach here if preferred. Sam

attachments: aws-adjustment-report-3456.csv
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <accounts-payable@nebulaops.com>, Sam Chen <sam.chen@amazon.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jul 2025 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Negative invoice applied to our account - urgent hold request

Forwarding AWS response and adjustment report. Proposed immediate plan: 
1) Hold payout for NebulaOps tranche (Finance ops) until mapping confirmed — Marissa please enact hold and log in payout tracker.
2) Redwood to request AWS JSON metering payload and provide to NebulaOps for joint reconciliation (Marcus will coordinate).
3) If AWS confirms the credit was applied to seller account 9012345678 but NebulaOps shows US vs EU mismatch, Redwood will issue a corrective reallocation credit in our ledger and provide NebulaOps with a signed credit note for their records.
4) Naomi: prepare a brief note (one-pager) on VAT implications in case the credit needs to be reallocated to EU entity (include required documentation: VAT id, registration cert).
5) Target: confirm final allocation by EOD Friday 2025-07-25 so NebulaOps can close month-end.

Marissa: assign to payment-ops queue and tag escrow/hold. Jonas: flag potential revenue-recognition impact and estimate P&L delta. I'll set a 2pm PT sync tomorrow if needed.

Regards,
Marcus
Revenue Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
